To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) in patients with LPL deficiency, the conversion of VDL to LDL is normal; and (2) the relative capacities of LPL and hepatic lipases to hydrolyse TG in VLDL are similar, but the capacity of hepatic lipases is much greater than that of LPL in IDL.

(a) hepatic lipase has a higher affinity than LPL for VLDL, and a higher activity against IDL than VLDL; and (b) in patients with non-functioning lipoprotein LPL, hepatic lipolysis is not impaired, and hepatic lipolase plays a significant part in VLDL, especially IDL, metabolism.
hepatic lipose has a significant role in lipoprotein lipolysis and that it is especially important for intermediate density lipoprotein lipolytic clearance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the metabolism of very low‐density lipoprotein and low‐density lipo‐protein in normal and abnormal states.
the roles of hepatic lipoprotein lipoprotein lipases in the metabolism of triglyceride rich lipoproteins.
the metabolism of lipoproteins and lipids in health and disease, and in particular the role played by lipoprotein lipases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the roles of hepatic lipases and LPL are complementary, and that the former may be of greater importance than the latter in lipoprotein remnant metabolism.
hepatic lipases are involved in the catabolism of lipoprotein‐TG in man, especially in the catabolic pathway of VLDL and IDL.
hepatic lipases play a major role in lipoprotein remodelling and turnover, but the relative contributions of LPL and hepatic lipases vary with the type of lipoprotein and its size.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

hepatic lipases play an important role in the metabolism of VLDL and IDL, and that the relative contribution of LPL and hepatic lipases to VLDL and VLDL‐remnant metabolism is dependent on the particle size of the substrate.
hepatic lipolysis is a key step in the metabolism of VLDL and its remnants, and that it is probably more important than the removal of VLDL remnants by the liver.

hepatic lipoprotein lipoprotein lipolytic activity in the circulation is not only dependent on the presence of the enzyme, but is also dependent on the substrate lipoprotein particle size and the lipoprotein TG concentrations in the circulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lipoprotein lipolytic enzyme, hepatic lipases, plays a significant role on VLDL and VLDL remnants metabolism, especially IDL, at least in the absence of lipoprotein lipidase.
the hepatic lipase is a significant player in lipoprotein clearance.
hepatic lipolysis is not a trivial issue and that hepatic lipolytic capacity should be considered in the interpretation of the lipolytic activity in post-heparin plasma.
